reviews.review: Rogue-lite with smooth movement and satisfying gun-play, not a lot of content but what's there right now is amazing.

An FPS rougelite (rougelike? idk) with a charming art style, unique weapons and loadouts, buttery-smooth controls, a killer soundtrack, many many meaningful and permanent upgrades.
I've beaten what is available in terms of levels and bosses, but I still have things to unlock. Running through all the levels, you're showered with guns that match the environment you're in. Starting with rusty and cobbled together rifles and shotguns and transitioning into sleek, manufactured tools. With a mid-run upgrade system similar to that of Dead Cells, each run feels like through the RNG of the genre, you're still in control.

This review was written in early access, with the current version of the game at time of writing being 0.5.3-325. There is not a "final boss" implemented yet, with each successful run ending in a "To be continued..." without a cutscene. It's the nature of an early access title, I suppose, though it feels abrupt as it is now.
My biggest suggestion that I feel isn't something involved in finishing the game is an upgrade system for your guns. If you find a gun that you like, with an affix/effect roll you like early in your run, you will likely have to abandon it if not in the next biome, then the one after that. On the one hand, the sense of juggling guns means that runs don't feel homogenized in the moment-to-moment. But on the other, this means that you may have to abandon a gun that you find synergizes really well with the perk and upgrade build you have mad for yourself. I have no other way to describe how it feels to do that other than "not good."

Overall, the game runs beautifully, crashes possibly caused by early access aside. Each run feels unique, and even if it isn't a successful run, it still feels meaningful. I will definitely be supporting this game as it gets closer into full release.
